findings.evidence: The repo already annotates the exactly analogous characterisation of a `Prop`-valued def: `EpsilonEridani/QFT/Scattering/Photoproduction/Kinematics/Basic.lean:95-96` `@[simp] theorem isReal_iff (k : PhotonKinematics) : k.IsReal ↔ k.virtuality = 0 := (Iff.rfl)`. `@[grind]` occurs nowhere in `EpsilonEridani/`, so simp is the right annotation here.
findings.fix: Mark `parity_eq_one_iff`, `parity_eq_neg_one_iff` and `pauliAllowed_iff_odd` `@[simp]`. Leave `parity_def`, `exchangeSign_def` and `pauliAllowed_def` unannotated: `parity_def` as `@[simp]` would preempt `parity_eq_one_iff` on `c.parity`, and `pauliAllowed_def` competes with `pauliAllowed_iff_odd` on the same LHS.
findings.issue: The characteristic lemmas carry no automation annotation: `parity_eq_one_iff` (139), `parity_eq_neg_one_iff` (142) and `pauliAllowed_iff_odd` (169) are the normal forms — every selection theorem in the file opens with `rw [parity_eq_one_iff, ...]` / `rw [pauliAllowed_iff_odd, ...]` (lines 199, 210-211, 225-227, 247, 257) — yet only the six trivial projections `tripletS1_S`..`tripletD1_J` are `@[simp]`. Every downstream consumer must hand-rewrite to get at a channel's parity or Pauli status.

findings.evidence: Lines 107-113 (`-- The derived decision procedure is exposed so that `decide` can compare concrete channels in importing modules.` / `@[expose] section` / `deriving instance DecidableEq for ChannelLabel`) versus line 174 (`instance : Decidable (c.PauliAllowed T) := decidable_of_iff' _ (c.pauliAllowed_iff_odd T)`), which has no such attribute. The file is otherwise `public section` without `@[expose]`.
findings.fix: Pick one: add `@[expose]` to the `Decidable (PauliAllowed)` instance so both decision procedures evaluate downstream, or drop the `@[expose] section` around the `deriving instance DecidableEq` if it is not needed.
findings.issue: Inconsistent `@[expose]` on the two decision procedures. The `DecidableEq ChannelLabel` instance is wrapped in `@[expose] section` (lines 107-113) with the comment that this is what lets `decide` compare concrete channels in importing modules, but `instance : Decidable (c.PauliAllowed T)` (line 174) is left unexposed. If the comment is right, `decide` on `PauliAllowed` does not reduce downstream — contradicting the stated design and the `Main definitions` claim that `PauliAllowed` is usable by computation; if instance bodies are exported anyway, the `@[expose] section` is a body exposed for no reason and must go.

summary: The surface is minimal, bodies are hidden, and the characteristic lemmas (`parity_def`, `exchangeSign_def`/`exchangeSign_eq`, `pauliAllowed_def`/`pauliAllowed_iff_odd`) are present, with no compatibility artifacts. Two defects: none of the characteristic lemmas carry `@[simp]`, and the `@[expose]` treatment of the two decision procedures is inconsistent.
